memory_lessons.applicability: Use the measured two-launch schedule as the comparison point when evaluating a larger tile; it does not establish that the parent tile is optimal.
memory_lessons.claim: The parent candidate was controller-valid on all 10 supplied cases and measured 16.9348 μs mean versus the 46.7866 μs baseline; the catalog reports only one distinct T2 program so far.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure the 2048-input tile against the parent using full-domain correctness and the total-run timing protocol.

proposal.hypothesis: Doubling the large-path tile from 1024 to 2048 inputs per CTA should halve the first-stage partial count (4096 to 2048 at n=4194304) and final-CTA reads while preserving the existing CTA reduction and two-launch direct-output schedule. This tests whether the lower first-stage CTA count still provides sufficient parallelism; correctness and total-run performance remain for controller evaluation.

retained: Increase large-path work per CTA from 1024 to 2048 elements using the same 128-thread shared-memory reduction.
Adjust first-stage block count to produce ceil(n/2048) partials; retain one final CTA that reads those initialized partials and writes directly to out.
